title: In Christ
subtitle: What the Bible says about the place where you now live

key_verse.text: Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.

cards.title: No one starts on neutral ground
cards.subtitle: Paul builds all of Romans 5 on this single comparison
cards.content:
There is a question the Bible answers before we even think to ask it: where do I actually stand before God?

Paul devotes an entire chapter to the answer. In Romans 5, he constructs a comparison that covers everything:

⚖️ TWO POSITIONS. TWO REPRESENTATIVES. TWO DESTINIES:

On one side: Adam. On the other: Christ.

Not as distant historical figures, but as federal heads — representatives. Every human being who enters this world is born into one of these two positions. There is no third option. There is no neutral ground.

Adam stood for humanity in the garden. When he fell, all who were in him fell with him. Paul states it unflinchingly: 'Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned.' (Romans 5:12)

This is not God punishing us for what someone else did; it is because we were in him. We were bound to him the way a branch is bound to the vine it grows from.

✝️ BUT THEN CAME THE SECOND ADAM:

Romans 5:17 says: 'For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.'

What Adam dragged downward, Christ lifts upward. The same logic, the same representation — but moving in the opposite direction.

🔑 THE PRACTICAL QUESTION:

So the question is not 'Am I a good person?' The question is 'In whom am I?'

Being in Adam doesn't mean being monstrous. It can look like being polite, generous, or even deeply religious. But it means being connected to a root that produces death — no matter how hard the branch tries.

Being in Christ means the root has changed. It's not about the branch trying harder, but about drawing from an entirely different source. And that difference works its way outward from the inside.

That transfer happens the moment a person truly believes and is born again. It is not a gradual process or a goal to work toward — it is a single, decisive step. 'Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.' (1 Peter 1:23)

scripture_references.text: Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned.
For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.

Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God. Nicodemus saith unto him, How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter the second time into his mother's womb, and be born? Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.

cards.revelation_key: The most important question is not how well you are living, but whose you are. In Adam or in Christ — there is no third place.

cards.title: Logizomai: The day you switched ledgers
cards.subtitle: Romans 6:11 — an accounting word that explains the true nature of conversion
cards.content:
In Romans 6:11, Paul reaches for a word his first-century readers would have recognized instantly from the world of commerce and finance:

λογίζομαι — logizomai.

It is not a religious or technical term. It is a bookkeeping word. It means to reckon, to record in the ledger, to enter a fact as settled and final.

📒 WHAT A FIRST-CENTURY ACCOUNTANT DID WITH THIS WORD:

When a Greek accountant in the first century used logizomai, he was saying: 'This has already happened. It is entered in the book. It is no longer in dispute.'

It was not a wish. Not a goal. It was a fact set down in writing.

✝️ WHAT PAUL DOES WITH IT:

'Likewise reckon ye also yourselves to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord.' (Romans 6:11)

The word 'reckon' is logizomai. Paul is saying: enter this in your inner ledger as a fact already accomplished.

What fact? That your old life — the one rooted in Adam, under the current of sin — died with Christ on the cross. And that the life you now have is in Him.

🔍 WHY THIS MATTERS IN DAILY LIFE:

Many believers live as if their standing before God is still being negotiated. As if the account is still open. As if the verdict could change.

Logizomai says: the account is closed. The transfer already happened. You are not trying to get into Christ — if you have believed and been born again, you are already inside.

The problem is not the position. The problem is that many have never entered it in their inner ledger as a settled fact.

Saving faith doesn't wait to feel the reality before believing it — it records the reality first, and experience follows.

greek_words.meaning: To reckon, to count as settled, to record in the ledger as a completed and certain fact
greek_words.revelation: Paul does not say 'try to feel dead to sin.' He says 'reckon it as done.' Saving faith does not wait for the feeling to confirm the reality — it records the reality first, and the experience follows.

scripture_references.text: Likewise reckon ye also yourselves to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord.

I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.

cards.revelation_key: You are not fighting to get into Christ. If you believed and were born again, you are already in. The missing step is not more effort — it is entering that fact in your inner ledger as something already done and final.

cards.title: Jesus did not say 'visit me.' He said 'stay.'
cards.subtitle: John 15 — the difference between passing through a place and living there
cards.content:
Some believers merely visit Christ. They go to church, read the Bible occasionally, pray when things get hard. But visiting is not the same as dwelling.

Jesus was very specific about what He wanted. In John 15, He repeats the same command again and again: 'Abide in me.'

Not 'come by sometimes.' Not 'think of me now and then.' Abide. Stay. Make this place your home.

🌱 THE IMAGE HE CHOSE:

'I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman... Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.' (John 15:1, 4)

Jesus did not choose the image of a building you walk in and out of. He chose the image of a branch and a vine.

A branch doesn't visit the vine. The branch is in the vine. It doesn't decide each morning whether to reconnect. The connection is its normal condition, its very mode of existence.

🔍 WHAT JESUS TIES TO ABIDING:

In verse 7 He says: 'If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you...'
In verse 10 He says: 'If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love.'

Two concrete things: His Word and obedience to His commands.

These are not requirements for entry — they are how a branch stays alive. The branch that fails to draw sap dries out. Not as a punishment, but by its very nature.

⚠️ THE DIRECT WARNING:

'If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered.' (John 15:6)

Jesus is not speaking here of people who never knew Him. He is speaking of branches that fail to remain connected. That disconnection is rarely dramatic. Often, it's incredibly gradual — less time in the Word, less prayer, more noise, until one day the branch bears no fruit and cannot understand why.

But a diagnosis is not a condemnation. If you recognize dryness in your life as you read this, that very recognition is a signal that the Vine is calling you back. A dead branch feels nothing. The one who feels the dryness is still alive — and can still return.

scripture_references.text: Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me. I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you.

cards.revelation_key: The Christian life is not a series of visits to God in moments of need. It is living in Him the way a branch lives in the tree — continuously, without interruption, drawing everything from the root.

cards.title: Seeing life from the floor where you now live
cards.subtitle: Colossians 3 — your position changes the vantage point from which you read everything
cards.content:
Imagine you live on the ground floor of a building in a flooded city. From your window you see water, debris, and chaos. Everything you see tells you the situation is hopeless.

Now imagine someone takes you to the tenth floor. From there you still see the flood — but you also see the roads that are dry, the rescue teams moving in, the horizon where the water ends.

The situation did not change. The floor you are standing on did.

🏔️ WHAT PAUL SAYS IN COLOSSIANS:

'If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God. Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth. For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God.' (Colossians 3:1-3)

Paul does not say 'try not to worry.' He says something more concrete: you have already risen with Christ. You are already seated with Him. Your real life — the life God sees — is hidden with Christ in God.

That is not poetry. That is a position.

🔑 WHAT CHANGES WHEN YOU LIVE FROM THAT POSITION:

The crises do not disappear. The pain does not disappear. But they are viewed from an entirely different vantage point.

Fear about the future, viewed from the ground floor, paralyzes. Viewed from where Christ is seated, it says: 'I am in the hands of the One who already knows how this ends.'

This is not denial. It is reading reality from the right floor.

💬 A QUESTION WORTH SITTING WITH:

When a crisis comes, which floor are you looking at it from? And if you can't feel it right now — remember His promise: 'Lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.' (Matthew 28:20) He didn't say, 'only when you feel me.' He said *always*.

scripture_references.text: If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God. Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth. For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God.
And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus.
Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.

cards.revelation_key: Your position in Christ is not a comforting idea for hard moments. It is the real floor from which you are called to read every moment of your life — including the darkest ones.

cards.title: Fruit is not manufactured. It grows.
cards.subtitle: The evidence of being in Christ is not your effort — it is what flows out naturally
cards.content:
There is a very common trap in the Christian life: trying to manufacture the fruit.

You see the list of the fruit of the Spirit — love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance (Galatians 5:22-23) — and you turn it into a to-do list. Try harder to be patient. Decide to be more loving. Work up more joy.

The problem is that fruit does not work that way.

🍎 WHAT NO APPLE TREE DOES:

An apple tree does not strain to produce apples. It makes no decisions about it. It sets no annual production goals. Apples are simply the natural result of being an apple tree with healthy roots and enough water.

If an apple tree bears no fruit, the problem is not in the branch. It is in the root, or the lack of water.

John says it plainly: 'He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.' (1 John 2:6)

He does not say 'he who tries harder.' He says 'he that abideth.'

⚠️ THE CONFRONTATION THAT CANNOT BE AVOIDED:

At the same time, the image of fruit is the one that most directly confronts a lukewarm Christian life.

Jesus said in Matthew 7:16: 'Ye shall know them by their fruits.'

In the ancient world, fruit was the legal proof of a tree's nature. You did not need to see the roots to know what you were dealing with. You simply looked at what it produced.

A person who claims to be in Christ but whose life is still governed by unreleased bitterness, or whose heart is completely divided — that person isn't being judged by their words; they are being revealed by their fruit.

Not as condemnation. As diagnosis.

🌱 THE GOOD NEWS:

If the problem is the root, the answer is not more effort. The answer is more abiding. More Word. More daily obedience. More time in the Vine, who is Jesus Christ.

And if sin has disrupted that connection — there is a direct way back: 'If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.' (1 John 1:9) It does not say 'if you deserve it.' It says 'if we confess.'

Fruit grows only when the branch is well connected. That is both the promise and the responsibility we must hold at the same time.

scripture_references.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.
Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

cards.identity_statement: You are not someone who strains to produce spiritual fruit through sheer will. You are a branch connected to the true Vine. Your work is to abide. The fruit is His responsibility.
cards.revelation_key: The fruit of the Spirit is not a list of things you must achieve. It is a description of what naturally grows in a life that stays connected to Christ.

discovery_questions.question: Paul says your life is 'hid with Christ in God' — not as a future promise, but as a present reality. Is there an area of your life where you are still looking at your situation from the ground floor, forgetting the floor where you actually live?

Jesus draws a clear line between visiting and dwelling. Being honest with yourself — does your relationship with Christ right now look more like someone living in their own home, or someone passing through as a guest?
Fruit is not manufactured — it grows when the root is healthy. Is there fruit you have been trying to produce through your own effort, rather than seeking it through greater abiding in Christ?

prayer.title: Prayer from the inside
prayer.content:
Lord, thank You that You do not ask me to reach You from the outside. You ask me to live from the inside — from the place You already put me when I believed.

I confess that I often live as if I were still on the outside. Viewing my life from the wrong floor. Visiting You instead of dwelling in You. Trying to produce by my own effort what only grows when I am well connected to You.

Today I want to settle this in my heart as a fact: I am in Christ. My life is hidden with You in God. That does not change with my emotions or my circumstances.

Help me to live from that place. To read Your Word not as an obligation but as the sap that keeps me alive. To obey You not out of fear but because I am a branch that wants to bear fruit.

Let my life be evidence that the root is good — not through my striving, but through Your presence in me.

Thank You that You do not depend on my effort to sustain me. Thank You that when I fell, You did not let go. Thank You that the same Spirit who raised Christ from the dead lives in me — and that does not change with my circumstances or my failures.

Today I receive it as a fact: I am Yours, I am in You, and Your Word that does not return void holds me.

In the name of Jesus, Amen.
